**What changed:** In Angular 21.0.0, `NgModuleFactory` has been removed; the changelog lists under **common → Breaking Changes**: "NgModuleFactory has been removed, use NgModule instead." (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/21.0.0/CHANGELOG.md). The removal was done in PR #62838 "refactor(common): remove `ngModuleFactory` input of `NgComponentOutlet`", whose breaking-change note repeats: "NgModuleFactory has been removed, use NgModule instead." The `ngModuleFactory` input of `NgComponentOutlet` had been deprecated by PR #44815, which "updates the logic of the `NgComponentOutlet` class to allow passing an `NgModule` as an input instead of passing NgModule factory." (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62838, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/44815)

**Affects:** Applications that import `NgModuleFactory` from `@angular/common`/`@angular/core` (e.g. via `compileModuleAsync`/`NgModuleFactory.type`) or that bind the `ngModuleFactory` input of `NgComponentOutlet` / pass an `NgModuleFactory` to it.

**Action:** required: remove all imports and usages of `NgModuleFactory`; where an `NgModuleFactory` was passed to `NgComponentOutlet`, pass the `NgModule` class itself instead (via the `ngModule` input / `NgComponentOutlet` binding). Re-verify dynamically created components still render.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before: NgComponentOutlet with the removed ngModuleFactory input -->
<ng-template *ngComponentOutlet="{ content: [], ngModuleFactory: myModuleFactory }"></ng-template>

<!-- after: pass the NgModule itself -->
<ng-template *ngComponentOutlet="myNgModule"></ng-template>
```

**What changed:** The `ignoreChangesOutsideZone` flag on `NgZoneChangeDetectionScheduler` (the `ÉµNgZoneChangeDetectionScheduler` class used to configure ZoneJS change detection behavior) was removed in Angular v21 by PR 62700 "fix(core): Remove ignoreChangesOutsideZone option", labeled `target: major` and `detected: breaking change` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62700). It had originally been introduced in v18 as an opt-out for the new behavior that scheduled change detection even when events occurred outside the `NgZone`, and was deprecated in v18.2 by PR 57029 "fix(core): Deprecate `ignoreChangesOutsideZone` option" (https://github.com/angular/angular/pulls?q=is%3Apr+ignoreChangesOutsideZone). Per the removal commit message: "After monitoring the results post-release, we have determined that this feature is working as desired and do not believe it should ever be disabled by setting this option to `true`." The changelog entry reads: "BREAKING CHANGE: `ignoreChangesOutsideZone` is no longer available as an option for configuring ZoneJS change detection behavior." (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62700)

**Affects:** Applications that set `ignoreChangesOutsideZone: true` when providing the ZoneJS change-detection scheduler (`ÉµNgZoneChangeDetectionScheduler`), e.g. via `providers`/`NG_CHANGE_DETECTION_SCHEDULER`-style provider config.

**Action:** required: delete the `ignoreChangesOutsideZone` property from any `ÉµNgZoneChangeDetectionScheduler` provider configuration; change detection scheduling for events outside `NgZone` can no longer be opted out of, so re-verify that app behavior does not rely on `ignoreChangesOutsideZone: true` semantics (i.e. no change detection scheduled for out-of-zone events).

**Before/after:**
```ts
// No code snippet for this option appears on the fetched pages (PR text only).
```

**What changed:** In `@angular/elements`, custom-element input getters were standardized in Angular 21. Previously, signal inputs (`input()`) on a custom element returned the signal function from the property getter, so consumers had to call `elementRef.newInput()`, while decorator `@Input()` properties returned the value directly (`elementRef.oldInput`). Setters were always assignment-style for both (`elementRef.newInput = 'new value'`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/62097). Angular 21.0.0 lists this under Breaking Changes → elements: "Fix signal input getter behavior in custom elements… The getter behavior has been standardized so signal inputs can now be accessed directly, matching the behavior of decorator inputs: Before: Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`, Signal Input: `elementRef.newInput()`; After: Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`, Signal Input: `elementRef.newInput`" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/refs/tags/21.0.0/CHANGELOG.md). Fix implemented in PR #62113 / commit `be0455adda`, "fix(elements): return value on signal input getter" (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62113). Note the title's "Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`" is the *unchanged* side of this breaking change; decorator `@Input` behavior is identical before and after — the change applies only to signal inputs.

**Affects:** Applications using `@angular/elements` `createCustomElement` with components that declare signal inputs (`input()` / `input.required()` / `model()`), where the created element instance's properties are read from outside (e.g. `elementRef.newInput()` in app code, tests, or third-party JS).

**Action:** required: remove the call parens when reading signal-input properties off a custom element instance — read `elementRef.newInput` instead of `elementRef.newInput()`. Assignment (`elementRef.newInput = 'value'`) and template/attribute binding are unchanged. Re-verify any code that relied on the getter returning a `Signal` (e.g. passing `elementRef.newInput` as a signal, or calling effects/computed on it), since it now returns the value.

**Before/after:**
```text
Before:
- Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`
- Signal Input: `elementRef.newInput()`

After:
- Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`
- Signal Input: `elementRef.newInput`
```
(https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/be0455adda7d92f741105b3599e7922f099cc024)

I have the authoritative release-note facts; stopping here.

**What changed:** In `@angular/elements`, signal inputs on custom elements had inconsistent getter behavior: reading an input off the custom element required calling it as a function (`elementRef.newInput()`) while decorator-based `@Input`s were read directly (`elementRef.oldInput`). Angular 21.0.0 standardized the getter so signal inputs are now accessed directly, like decorator inputs — Before: "Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`, Signal Input: `elementRef.newInput()`"; After: "Decorator Input: `elementRef.oldInput`, Signal Input: `elementRef.newInput`". The v21 release notes list this under **Breaking Changes → elements**: "Fix signal input getter behavior in custom elements." (https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/21.0.0)

**Affects:** Applications that use `@angular/elements` (`createCustomElement`) with components declaring signal inputs via `input()`, and that read those input values from the custom element instance from outside the component (e.g. `myEl.someSignalInput()` in JS/TS or host code).

**Action:** required: Remove the trailing call `()` when reading signal input values off a custom element instance; `elementRef.someSignalInput` now returns the value directly instead of the signal function. Also re-verify any code that relied on the old callable behavior (e.g. passing `el.someSignalInput` around as a function, or `untracked`-style reads through the element).

**Before/after:**
```text
Before:
  Decorator Input: elementRef.oldInput
  Signal Input: elementRef.newInput()

After:
  Decorator Input: elementRef.oldInput
  Signal Input: elementRef.newInput
```
(quoted from https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/21.0.0)

**What changed:** Angular 21.0.0 adds a new reactive directive `FormArrayDirective` (exported from `@angular/forms`, declared in `ReactiveFormsModule`/`ɵmod`) with selector `[formArray]` and input alias `formArray` binding a top-level `FormArray`, plus `(ngSubmit)` output, and a new public abstract base class `AbstractFormDirective` which `FormGroupDirective` now extends (BREAKING CHANGE from the PR: the `formDirective` getter on `FormGroupName` and `FormArrayName` now returns `AbstractFormDirective` instead of `FormGroupDirective | null`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/55880, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/21.0.0/CHANGELOG.md). The v21 breaking-change entry for `forms` reads: "This new directive will conflict with existing FormArray directives or formArray inputs on the same element." (`NgControlStatusGroup`'s selector gained `[formArray]`, and `NgForm`'s selector became `form:not([ngNoForm]):not([formGroup]):not([formArray]),ng-form,[ngForm]`, so a `<form [formArray]>` no longer gets `NgForm`.)

**Affects:** templates of `ReactiveFormsModule` apps where an element already has an input/attribute named `formArray` (custom component `[formArray]`/`formArray` input, a directive matching `[formArray]`, or a repeated/legacy `FormArray` directive) — those now also match `FormArrayDirective`.

**Action:** required: remove/rename the conflicting `formArray` input or directive selector on elements handled by other components/directives (e.g. rename the custom input), or keep the element out of `[formArray]` matching; re-verify that existing `<form>` templates without `[formArray]` still receive `NgForm` and that `NgControlStatusGroup` status classes on `[formArray]` elements are as intended. Re-verify code reading `FormArrayName.formDirective` / `FormGroupName.formDirective` now typed as `AbstractFormDirective`.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before: only NgForm applied to this form -->
<form [formArray]="formArray"> ... </form>

<!-- after v21: matches the new FormArrayDirective (selector "[formArray]"),
     NgForm selector is now:
     form:not([ngNoForm]):not([formGroup]):not([formArray]),ng-form,[ngForm] -->
```

**What changed:** In Angular 21.0.0 the `@angular/router` package reports that "Router navigations may take several additional microtasks to complete" compared to 20.3. The changelog notes that tests are "often highly dependent on the exact timing of navigation completions with respect to the microtask queue" and that, on rare occasions, production applications are affected when "multiple subscriptions to router state throughout the application, both of which trigger navigations that happened to not conflict with the previous timing" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/21.0.0/CHANGELOG.md, "Breaking Changes > router"). The same router block also lists a separate change: "`lastSuccessfulNavigation` is now a signal and needs to be invoked" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/21.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).

**Affects:** Applications that depend on the exact number/timing of microtasks after a navigation (e.g. tests making router-state assertions after only a few `tick()` calls), and tests that assert immediately after a navigation. Also affects reads of `Router.lastSuccessfulNavigation`, which is now a signal.

**Action:** required: re-verify timing-sensitive router tests; the changelog's stated fix is "to ensure all navigations have been completed before making assertions." Re-verify any code that reads `Router.lastSuccessfulNavigation` because it now requires invoking the signal. No concrete code/config/build change is given in the fetched sources.

**Before/after:** (no code or configuration snippet is present on the fetched pages; this is a behavioral timing change described only in prose, so no snippet is provided.)

**What changed:** In Angular 21.0.0, under the `zone.js` package's Breaking Changes, the changelog states: "IE/Non-Chromium Edge are not supported anymore." This drops legacy browser shims/workarounds from ZoneJS for Internet Explorer and legacy (pre-Chromium) Microsoft Edge, which are also no longer in Angular's supported browsers list (angular.io/guide/versions). (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/refs/tags/21.0.0/CHANGELOG.md)

**Affects:** Applications that must run in Internet Explorer or legacy non-Chromium Edge (EdgeHTML), and applications that relied on ZoneJS's legacy-browser patches — e.g. projects configured with a browserslist targeting `ie` or legacy Edge, or that included the legacy ZoneJS events/webapis patches for those browsers. Applications targeting only modern browsers are unaffected.

**Action:** none — no code, dependency or configuration change is required for apps not supporting IE/legacy Edge; applications still needing to run in those browsers cannot upgrade and must remain on Angular 20.x, or re-verify the app's behavior in supported browsers only.

**Before/after:**
```text
# .browserslistrc — legacy targets are no longer supported by ZoneJS in v21
ie 11                 # remove
edge 18               # remove (non-Chromium Edge)
```

**What changed:** In Angular 21.0.0, `TestBed` now provides a fake `PlatformLocation` implementation that supports the Navigation API by default, whereas `TestBed` previously provided the old default implementation. This new fake is supplied via `ɵprovideFakePlatformNavigation()` from `@angular/common/testing`, which `BrowserTestingModule` adds to its providers (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/21.0.x/packages/platform-browser/testing/src/browser.ts). The change also adds experimental support for the Navigation API in `@angular/common` as part of interop 2025 (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63406).

**Affects:** Applications with `TestBed`-based tests that rely on the previous default `PlatformLocation` test implementation, or that assert on location behavior during routing.

**Action:** required: re-verify test behavior around `PlatformLocation`/navigation; to revert to the old default, provide the `MockPlatformLocation` from `@angular/common/testing` in your providers (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63406).

**Before/after:**
```typescript
// Revert TestBed to the old default PlatformLocation:
{provide: PlatformLocation, useClass: MockPlatformLocation}
```

**What changed:** The `ngComponentOutletContent` input of `NgComponentOutlet` (package `@angular/common`) was retyped from `any[][] | undefined` to `Node[][] | undefined`. `any` was dropped "in favor of `Node` for better type safety and clarity"; `Node[][]` is what `ViewContainerRef.createComponent` (into which the input value is passed) actually expects (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63674, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7a4b225c57d8e390ec06731f5211d52d14da3a9c, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/63538). The change is flagged `breaking changes` / `target: major` and landed in the 21.0 major. This is a TypeScript type-only change: no runtime behaviour of `NgComponentOutlet` changes.

**Affects:** Applications that bind or pass a value to `ngComponentOutletContent` whose element type is not assignable to `Node[][]` (e.g. `string[][]`, plain-object arrays, or other non-`Node` projectable-node shapes such as `SelectorMatch[][]`/`string[]`-based projectable node definitions), and that type-check during build (`ng build` / `ng test`). Previously the `any[][]` type silently accepted these values.

**Action:** required: re-verify every usage of `ngComponentOutletContent` type-checks against `Node[][] | undefined`; values passed must be `Node` instances (or `undefined`), matching what `ViewContainerRef.createComponent` accepts. Note that DOM projectable-node definitions expressed as CSS selector strings are no longer type-accepted by this input — such values must be real `Node` objects (e.g. obtained via `document.querySelector` / template element cloning) for the array to type-check.

**Before/after:**
No code or configuration snippet is shown on the fetched commit, PR, or issue pages, so none is reproduced here. The type change itself, as stated verbatim in the commit message, is: `ngComponentOutletContent` is now of type `Node[][] | undefined` instead of `any[][] | undefined`.

**What changed:** In Angular 21.0.0, the deprecated `ngModuleFactory` input of `NgComponentOutlet` (`@angular/common`) was removed, along with `NgModuleFactory` support — "NgModuleFactory has been removed, use NgModule instead" (#62838, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/25f593ce2a623add0cbd4ab3bb0d4987793e4f34; https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62838). The input had been deprecated by PR #44815, which added `NgModule` class support as an alternative (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/44815). The v21 API reference for `NgComponentOutlet` now lists only these inputs: `ngComponentOutlet`, `ngComponentOutletInputs`, `ngComponentOutletInjector`, `ngComponentOutletEnvironmentInjector`, `ngComponentOutletContent`, and `ngComponentOutletNgModule` ("Optional NgModule class reference to allow loading another module dynamically, then loading a component from that module") — no `ngModuleFactory` (https://v21.angular.dev/api/common/NgComponentOutlet).

**Affects:** Applications using `NgComponentOutlet` with the `[ngComponentOutletNgModuleFactory]` binding / `ngModuleFactory` input, or passing an `NgModuleFactory` instance (e.g. from `@angular/platform-browser`'s `NgModuleFactory` / `compileNgModuleFactory`).

**Action:** required: replace the `ngModuleFactory` input with `ngComponentOutletNgModule`, passing the `NgModule` class reference directly instead of an `NgModuleFactory` instance.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before (NgModuleFactory input, removed in v21) -->
<ng-container *ngComponentOutlet="comp; ngModuleFactory: myModuleFactory"></ng-container>

<!-- after (v21 API) -->
<ng-container *ngComponentOutlet="comp; ngComponentOutletNgModule: myModule"></ng-container>
```

**What changed:** In Angular 20.3.11, PR #64509 replaced a regex-based approach for shimming `:host-context()` selectors (in `shadow_css.ts`) with a new parenthesis-aware generator function `_splitOnTopLevelCommas`, to support arbitrary nesting inside `:host-context()` (e.g. `:host-context(:is(.foo, .bar))`). This caused a regression (issue #65137): styles containing unbalanced closing parentheses inside declaration blocks — specifically quoted `background-image` urls — were truncated/"choked" on, because `_convertColonHostContext` traverses the entire declaration block when scanning for `:host-context()` selectors to shim. Commit `ecea909` (cherry-pick of `9e7ddca`) adds a new flag to `_splitOnTopLevelCommas` that lets it continue past unbalanced closing parentheses in the declaration block, returning `_convertColonHostContext` to its previous behavior while keeping the new arbitrary-nesting support in `:host-context()` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ecea909bccc3d6a3c33e77e1feb4ad0926e72f9e, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/64509, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/65137).

**Affects:** Applications whose component styles (including Less/SCSS-compiled CSS) contain unbalanced closing parentheses in quoted `background-image: url("...")` values — the symptom appeared only when building with `@angular/compiler` 20.3.11; it is fixed again in 21.0.0.

**Action:** none — the fix is included in 21.0.0; applications on 20.3.11 only need to confirm styles with quoted urls containing `)` render fully after the upgrade.

(No code/configuration snippet is available from the fetched pages — this was an internal parser change.)

**What changed:** The Angular template type-checking logic in `compiler-cli` (`packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/type_check_block.ts`, `TcbFieldDirectiveTypeBaseOp` / `TcbNativeFieldDirectiveTypeOp`) previously treated `value` as one of the unsupported bindings on signal-form `Field` directives (alongside `checked`, `errors`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `disabledReasons`, `name`, `readonly`, `touched`, `max`, `maxlength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `minLength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `required`, `type`), producing a template type error. Now, when the host element is `<input type="radio">`, `value` is removed from the unsupported set, so binding or setting `value` on radio controls is allowed (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/5b55200edfd12fa7dcdb6570885e0c52a9cc5ec0, patch view).

**Affects:** Applications using `@angular/forms/signals` `Field` (`form(...)`) on `<input type="radio">` elements with a `value` attribute or binding; previously these reported a template type-check diagnostic.

**Action:** none — this only removes a previously reported template type error; no code or configuration change is needed. Applications that had worked around the error can re-verify the radio `value` bindings type-check cleanly.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Previously reported as an unsupported binding on the field; now type-checks with no diagnostics -->
<form>
  <input type="radio" value="a" [field]="f">
  <input type="radio" value="b" [field]="f">
  <input type="radio" value="c" [field]="f">
</form>
```

**What changed:** The Angular template type checker (`compiler-cli`, `type_check_block.ts`) previously reported an error when a custom control directive used with signal forms had a required input (`value` or `checked`) that was not explicitly bound in the template. Now, when the `Field` directive from `@angular/forms/signals` is present on the same element, the checker skips reporting missing required `value` inputs (for a `FormValueControl`, i.e. a directive with a signal `value` input and `valueChange` output) and missing required `checked` inputs (for a `FormCheckboxControl`, signal `checked` input + `checkedChange` output), since `Field` binds these inputs implicitly (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/bd322ca4100c8e51df7c71377161c2c9412d1b83, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/165634264e5baca626f08097bf74ffb561a03468.patch). Implementation detail: `TcbDirectiveInputsOp` gains an `ignoredRequiredInputs` set populated via `isFieldDirective` and `getCustomFieldDirectiveType`.

**Affects:** Applications using signal forms (`@angular/forms/signals` `Field`) with custom control components/directives that declare required `value` (`model.required`) or `checked` inputs and are used with `[field]` binding without explicitly binding `value`/`checked`. This is a bug fix that removes false-positive template diagnostics; it does not introduce new errors.

**Action:** none — no code or configuration change is needed; previously "missing required input" errors for these cases simply disappear after upgrading.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- With Field present, no missing-input error is reported anymore -->
<custom-control [field]="f"/>

<!-- before (20.3.x): diagnostic that required input "value" is not bound
     after (21.0.0): no diagnostics -->
```
(Test case from https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/165634264e5baca626f08097bf74ffb561a03468.patch: `CustomControl implements FormValueControl<string> { readonly value = model.required<string>(); }`)

**What changed:** The Angular compiler-cli now emits a new template diagnostic when a property binding targets a state property managed automatically by the signal-forms `Field` directive. A new `ErrorCode` `FORM_FIELD_UNSUPPORTED_BINDING = 8022` was added, raised by `formFieldUnsupportedBinding` in `OutOfBandDiagnosticRecorderImpl` (`packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/oob.ts`) from `TcbFieldDirectiveTypeOp.execute()` in `type_check_block.ts`, which checks `BindingType.Property` inputs against a reserved list: `value`, `checked`, `errors`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `disabledReasons`, `name`, `readonly`, `touched`, `max`, `maxLength`, `min`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `required` (). Message: `Binding to '<name>' is not allowed on nodes using the [field] directive`. These names are reserved because the `Field` directive binds them itself from the bound `FieldTree`, per the `FormUiControl` contract in `packages/forms/signals/src/api/control.ts`; that file also states a `FormValueControl` "must not define a `checked` property" and a `FormCheckboxControl` "must not define a `value` property". Cherry-picked into 21.0.0 as `c371251e4c` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/c371251e4c2e7bc1ab6da7c51b05e047bdfe6068).

**Affects:** Templates where a node carries the signal-forms `Field` directive (or a `@if`/`@for`-style host element for it) and also has a property binding `[...]` for one of the reserved names above. Previously such bindings compiled; now they are a compile-time error (NG8022), so builds that succeeded on 20.3 can start failing.

**Action:** required: remove the offending property bindings from nodes using the `Field` directive (`[value]`, `[checked]`, `[errors]`, `[invalid]`, `[disabled]`, `[disabledReasons]`, `[name]`, `[readonly]`, `[touched]`, `[max]`, `[maxLength]`, `[min]`, `[minLength]`, `[pattern]`, `[required]`); these are set automatically by `Field` from the bound field state. For checkbox controls do not declare a `value` property, and for value controls do not declare a `checked` property. Re-verify that custom form control components integrating with `Field` only expose the contract inputs listed in `FormUiControl`/`FormValueControl`/`FormCheckboxControl`.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before: compiled on 20.3, now NG8022 -->
<my-input [field]="field()" [disabled]="isDisabled()" [required]="isRequired()" />

<!-- after: Field binds these from the field state itself -->
<my-input [field]="field()" />
```
```ts
// reserved names checked by TcbFieldDirectiveTypeOp (type_check_block.ts)
private invalidBindingNames = new Set([
  'value', 'checked', 'errors', 'invalid', 'disabled', 'disabledReasons',
  'name', 'readonly', 'touched', 'max', 'maxLength', 'min', 'minLength',
  'pattern', 'required',
]);
// error: FORM_FIELD_UNSUPPORTED_BINDING = 8022
// "Binding to '${node.name}' is not allowed on nodes using the [field] directive"
```

**What changed:** In 20.x, PR #62630 (a 20.x feature) made *all* ARIA property bindings write to the corresponding attribute, so `[ariaLabel]="expr"` compiled to `ɵɵattribute("aria-label", …)` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62630). Angular 21.0.0 commit `f008045ded` / PR #63925 partially reverts this: only property bindings whose target name begins with `aria-` are converted to attribute bindings (via new `isAriaAttribute` helper in `packages/compiler/src/template/pipeline/src/util/attributes.ts`); camelCase ARIA DOM properties are no longer renamed. So `[ariaLabel]` reverts to binding the `ariaLabel` DOM property (emitted as `ɵɵproperty`/`ɵɵdomProperty` instead of `ɵɵattribute`), while `[aria-label]` continues to bind the `aria-label` attribute. The `ariaAttrName()` name-mapping helper was removed from `reify.ts` and `packages/core/src/render3/instructions/aria_property.ts` (`ɵɵariaProperty` now writes the attribute name as given). The old behaviour broke properties whose value differs from the attribute value, e.g. `ariaLabelledByElements` (array of elements) vs `aria-labelledby` (ID string) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/f008045dedc773f70dd6f1ced73e689fb4436d6d, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63925). Note the only difference between `[aria-label]` and `[attr.aria-label]` is that the former will attempt to bind to directive inputs of the same name.

**Affects:** Applications that bind ARIA DOM properties using camelCase property-binding syntax (`[ariaLabel]`, `[ariaHasPopup]`, `[ariaLabelledByElements]`, etc.), in templates or in `host: {'[ariaLabel]': …}` host bindings, and that relied on the 20.x behaviour of these bindings rendering as HTML attributes (e.g. server-side rendering output, CSS/selectors or tests reading `getAttribute('aria-…')`).

**Action:** required: re-verify these bindings — from 21.0 they write the DOM property again, not the attribute; if the rendered attribute is required (e.g. for SSR HTML or attribute-based queries), switch to `[attr.aria-label]="expr"` or the dashed property syntax `[aria-label]="expr"`. Bindings already written as `[aria-label]` or `[attr.aria-label]`, and applications not binding camelCase ARIA properties, need no change.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Old 20.x behaviour: wrote the aria-label attribute -->
<!-- New 21.0 behaviour: writes the ariaLabel DOM property -->
<button [ariaLabel]="label"></button>

<!-- To keep attribute output in 21.0: -->
<button [aria-label]="label"></button>
<button [attr.aria-label]="label"></button>
```
```js
// Generated code change (compliance golden files in the commit):
// old: $r3$.ɵɵattribute("aria-label", ctx.label);
// new: $r3$.ɵɵproperty("ariaLabel", ctx.label);
```

**What changed:** Angular 21 added devmode-only Chrome DevTools custom formatters for Signals (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/64000). During review, the DevTools formatter config flag `skipFormatting` was renamed to `ngSkipFormatting`, but two usages in `packages/core/primitives/signals/src/formatter.ts` still passed `skipFormatting: true` when recursively formatting a signal's value (`['object', {object: sig, config: {...config, skipFormatting: true}}]` and in `prettifyPreview`), so recursive formatting was not skipped and caused "unfortunate UI recursion" in the DevTools console output. The fix (cherry-pick of commit 490435bf765dc4476e8ef4aad6eff122ff42bd34) replaced those with `ngSkipFormatting: true` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/c9f977833ebed6f89afd38f65c03e9b3808f2b07). This is entirely internal to Angular's signal formatter — it only affects how signals render in browser DevTools when Angular custom formatters are enabled in devmode, and PR 64000 itself notes "This change doesn't require a TGP, it doesn't affect existing code" (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/64000).

**What changed:** Angular 21.0.0 introduces an experimental signal-based forms API. Key components include the `form()` function, `Field` and `FieldState` objects, and a `[control]` directive for binding to UI elements. This API is designed to be signal-centric, using `WritableSignal` for a developer-owned data model rather than maintaining a copy of the data, and supports declarative logic via TypeScript schemas. It aims for interoperability with existing reactive forms (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/b8314bd3409500b8540d1ce00a330fdb2f0fc83a) (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63408). The API is described as experimental and does not yet support interop with Reactive/Template forms, dynamic objects, tuples, debouncing validation, or strongly-typed binding to UI controls (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/b8314bd3409500b8540d1ce00a330fdb2f0fc83a/packages/forms/signals/README.md).

**Affects:** All applications; however, existing template and reactive forms code remains unaffected and unchanged.

**Action:** none

**What changed:** In the signals forms API (`@angular/forms/signals`), the built-in validators `email`, `max`, `min`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, and `pattern` now return no error when the field value is "empty", using a shared internal `isEmpty` helper; previously they ran their checks against empty values (e.g. `email('')`, `minLength('', 10)`, `min(NaN, 10)` produced errors). Empty is defined as: `null`, `undefined`, `''`, `false`, or any number where `isNaN(value)` is true — i.e. `NaN` (note: `0` is not empty) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/10ef96adb3d989781c7ec5116a70b6518866ee27). This aligns them with native HTML validation and reactive forms validators. Exceptions that keep validating empty values: `required` (its purpose is non-empty), `validateStandardSchema` (schema decides), and `validate`/`validateAsync` (user logic decides) (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63456). Breaking API removal: the `emptyPredicate?: (value: TValue) => boolean` config option of `required(path, config)` was deleted; `required` now uses the standard `isEmpty` check (previously `false`, `''`, `null`, `undefined`), so e.g. `NaN` is now required-invalid but `0` is valid (commit diff, `goldens/public-api/forms/signals/index.api.md` and `required.ts`).

**Affects:** Apps using signals forms validators (`email`, `max`, `min`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `pattern`) whose models can hold `null`/`undefined`/`''`/`false`/`NaN` and which rely on those validators flagging such values as errors; and apps passing `emptyPredicate` to `required`.

**Action:** required: remove any `emptyPredicate` option passed to `required` (option no longer exists; the standard empty semantics now apply). Re-verify validation UI/flow for fields using `email`, `max`, `min`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `pattern` — empty values (`null`, `undefined`, `''`, `false`, `NaN`) are now valid; add `required` explicitly if a value must be present.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// Before (Angular 20.x signals forms): custom emptiness + empty-flagging validators
required(item.quantity, {emptyPredicate: (value) => value === 0});
minLength(p.text, 10); // '' -> minLengthError
min(p.age, 10);        // NaN -> minError

// After (21.0): required has only `when`/`error`; empties short-circuit validators
required(p.name);          // isEmpty: null | undefined | '' | false | NaN
minLength(p.text, 10);     // '' -> valid
min(p.age, 10);            // NaN -> valid
```

**What changed:** In signal forms (`@angular/forms/signals`), user interaction with a bound control now marks the field as dirty. Previously, when a field was bound to a native element (e.g. `<input [field]="f">`) or a custom `FormValueControl` component, typing into the control updated `state().value` but never called `state.markAsDirty()`, so `field().dirty()` stayed `false` — and `FormValueControl` implementers also had no way to mark dirty manually since `dirty` was only an input signal (issues #64465, #63623). The fix in `packages/core/src/render3/instructions/control.ts` calls `state.markAsDirty()` in both `listenToNativeControl`'s input listener and `listenToCustomControl`'s output listener, after `state.value.set(newValue)` (commit 3529877772, PR #64483). This was released as a `major`-target change.

**What changed:** The Angular Language Service VSCode extension's syntax highlighting for HTML templates changed how it handles interpolation and ICU messages within control flow block scopes. **Affects:** Applications and developers using the Angular Language Service VSCode extension when writing templates with Control Flow syntax (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) containing interpolation or ICU messages that rely on accurate syntax highlighting and bracket matching.

This was listed as a Breaking Change under `router` in the 21.0.0 release notes: "Router navigations may take several additional microtasks to complete. Tests have been found to often be highly dependent on the exact timing of navigation completions with respect to the microtask queue... On rare occasions, this can also affect production applications. This can be caused by multiple subscriptions to router state throughout the application, both of which trigger navigations that happened to not conflict with the previous timing." (https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/21.0.0, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62994). The PR is labeled `action: merge`, `area: router`, `target: major`, `detected: breaking change`. No public API signature of `Router` changed; the change is timing/stack-trace related (improved debugging with async/await stacks, better 1:1 with server-side recognize logic).

**Action:** required: re-verify navigation-timing-sensitive tests; ensure all navigations have completed before making assertions (the change's stated most common fix), and re-verify application behaviour in the rare case of multiple router-state subscriptions triggering navigations.
